schemes.label: Partita IVA

provenance.sourceText: «2. La fattura contiene le seguenti indicazioni: [...] d) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cedente o prestatore».

schemes.notes: DPR 26 ottobre 1972, n. 633, art. 21, comma 2, lettera d). Read directly at normattiva.it (https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21!vig=, plain HTTP response headed "vigente al 13/09/2026", curl with a browser User-Agent, no JS rendering needed), 2026-09-13. This binds the SELLER only ("cedente o prestatore") and carries no carve-out anywhere in comma 2 — a flat-rate/forfettario trader still holds and must state a Partita IVA. Cross-checked against the simplified-invoice regime at art. 21-bis, comma 1, lettera d) (same method/date, https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:decreto.del.presidente.della.repubblica:1972-10-26;633~art21bis!vig=): the seller's Partita IVA is NOT among the elements a simplified invoice (<=EUR100, raised to <=EUR400) may omit. Also cross-checked against the FatturaPA technical specification's own introduction, which restates the DPR 633/1972 list including "numero di partita IVA del cedente/prestatore" with no qualifier. For the SELLER this is genuinely unconditional — no VAT-regime carve-out exists. `required` is nonetheless set to `false` here, and this is the one deliberate departure from simply transcribing the seller's own unconditional rule: this catalog's ONLY axis is `appliesTo` (COMPANY/INDIVIDUAL/BOTH — the PARTY's own record type), and `resolveRequiredIdentifiers` takes no notion of transactional role at all. The exact same per-country array is read by `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` (always `partyType: "COMPANY"`, for the ACTIVE company about to issue invoices — i.e. always the SELLER in this product's outbound flow) AND by `client-upsert.tsx` (partyType taken from the CLIENT's own record type — i.e. the BUYER of that company's invoices). Setting `required: true` here would therefore ALSO become a hard block on saving an Italian, company-type CLIENT record — confirmed by reading client-upsert.tsx's `onSubmit` (a `required` scheme with an empty value calls `form.setError(...)` and `return`s, refusing to save) — but the BUYER-side rule is genuinely CONDITIONAL (DPR 633/1972 art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) — see this file's own LEGAL_ID entry below for the quote and the reasoning), not unconditional like the seller's. There is no per-role `required` in this schema, and the DB itself only allows one row per (countryCode, scheme) — `CountryIdentifierRequirement`'s unique key is `countryCode_scheme` — so a second "VAT" fact scoped to the buyer could not even coexist with this one; the seed would just overwrite it. `required: false` at country level is the same discipline this catalog already applies in fr.json/pt.json when a rule that IS mandatory for most sellers depends on a variable the catalog does not carry per party (there, the seller's own VAT regime; here, the party's ROLE in the transaction) — never a UI default, an explicit and documented choice. `appliesTo: 'COMPANY'` is similarly a simplification: an individual professional/sole trader acting as a business (an INDIVIDUAL record in this app) also holds and must state a Partita IVA when acting as a taxable person under this same lettera d) — but this choice is moot for the seller path specifically, because `onboarding.tsx`/`company.settings.tsx` always query `partyType: "COMPANY"` regardless of the active company's real legal form, so this fact is shown there unconditionally either way; it only affects whether an INDIVIDUAL-typed CLIENT also sees this field (optionally, since `required` is false here). FORMAT: the commonly-cited 11-digit numeric format for Partita IVA was NOT found in either DPR 633/1972 art. 21 or the FatturaPA Specifiche tecniche v1.4 (whose own `IdCodice` field states only a generic 28-character ceiling shared with foreign identifiers) — no `pattern` is declared here for that reason, the same discipline pt.json already applies to its own undeclared NIF/NIPC pattern.

schemes.label: Codice Fiscale

provenance.resolutionNote: Italian law does not always ask a buyer for the same document. A business buyer gives their VAT number (their Italian Partita IVA, or — if they are a business established elsewhere in the EU — their own country's VAT number instead). A buyer who is NOT acting as a business — typically a private individual — gives their Italian tax code (Codice Fiscale) instead of a VAT number. Right now this app has no way to tell those two situations apart for a given client: it only records whether a client is filed as a "Company" or an "Individual", and that is not the same thing as whether the client is acting as a VAT-registered business — an individual can run a business (and would then need to give a VAT number, not a tax code), and some companies are not VAT-registered (and would then need to give a tax code instead). Until a client record can say which of the two applies, this app cannot safely make either the VAT number or the Codice Fiscale mandatory here: doing so would sometimes ask a private individual for a business VAT number they will never have, or let a business through with neither number recorded. What would settle this: letting a client record say whether it is acting as a VAT-registered business, separately from whether it is filed as a Company or an Individual — once that exists, the correct one of the two identifiers can be safely required.

schemes.notes: DPR 633/1972, art. 21, comma 2, lettera f) (same page/method/date as the VAT entry above, 2026-09-13): the lettering repeats in the retrieved text — an "e)" covers the buyer's name/domicile and a first "f)" restates it, then a further "f)" (quoted here, semicolon-separated within the same point) states the actual number rule — quoted exactly as normattiva.it renders it, not tidied: «f) ditta, denominazione o ragione sociale, nome e cognome, residenza o domicilio del soggetto cessionario o committente, del rappresentante fiscale nonché ubicazione della stabile organizzazione per i soggetti non residenti; f) numero di partita IVA del soggetto cessionario o committente ovvero, in caso di soggetto passivo stabilito in un altro Stato membro dell'Unione europea, numero di identificazione IVA attribuito dallo Stato membro di stabilimento; nel caso in cui il cessionario o committente residente o domiciliato nel territorio dello Stato non agisce nell'esercizio d'impresa, arte o professione, codice fiscale;» Precisely: an Italian-established taxable-person buyer gives Partita IVA; a taxable person established in another EU Member State gives THEIR OWN state's VAT id, not an Italian Partita IVA; a buyer resident/domiciled in Italy who does NOT act in the exercise of a business, art or profession gives Codice Fiscale instead. Cross-validated by a second, independent primary source, the FatturaPA technical specification's own `CessionarioCommittente` block, which states the same alternative structurally: «IdFiscaleIVA (la valorizzazione di questi elementi è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento CodiceFiscale; in altri termini, possono non essere valorizzati se è valorizzato l'elemento CodiceFiscale; [...]) [...] CodiceFiscale: la valorizzazione di questo elemento è in alternativa non esclusiva a quella dell'elemento IdFiscaleIVA (può non essere valorizzato se è valorizzato l'elemento IdFiscaleIVA); consente l'inserimento del numero di codice fiscale del cessionario/committente.» (same PDF/URL as this file's VAT entry's own IT-3-equivalent citation — see this file's top-level `notes`). Also cross-validated by the simplified-invoice regime, art. 21-bis comma 1 lettera e): a simplified invoice can reduce the buyer's identification to "il solo codice fiscale o il numero di partita IVA" for an Italy-established buyer, the same CF/VAT alternative. `appliesTo: 'BOTH'` and `required: false` are both deliberate: BOTH because either a COMPANY-record or an INDIVIDUAL-record buyer can legally need either identifier depending on taxable-person status, not on record type (an INDIVIDUAL freelancer needs Partita IVA exactly like a COMPANY; a COMPANY-record entity that is not a taxable person would need Codice Fiscale exactly like a private INDIVIDUAL) — `appliesTo` cannot express that finer axis, so BOTH is the least wrong choice, not a claim that record type decides anything here. `required: false` because the rule is a genuine either/or conditioned on taxable-person status, which this catalog does not track per party (see this fact's own `resolutionNote`) — setting it `true` under either scheme name would demand a document some lawful buyers do not have. `provenance.kind` is `unverified` here NOT because the underlying law is in doubt (it is fully quoted above, read directly at normattiva.it) but because a fact this well-established in law, yet not safely enforceable by this product (the deciding variable, taxable-person status, exists nowhere in this app's data model) is recorded as `unverified` with a `resolutionNote` naming what the product would need, rather than graded `legal` with a `required` value that cannot honestly reflect a role-dependent rule. FORMAT: Codice Fiscale length IS established as 11-16 alphanumeric characters (Specifiche tecniche v1.4, §3.3.1, `DatiAnagraficiCedenteType`: «CodiceFiscale (Rif. par. 3.2): formato alfanumerico; lunghezza compresa tra 11 e 16 caratteri.», repeated identically for `RappresentanteFiscale` and `CessionarioCommittente`) — no `pattern` is declared on this fact regardless, by the same all-or-nothing discipline de.json's own VAT entry already uses (an unsourced claim elsewhere in the same fact keeps the whole fact from being promoted); if this fact is ever promoted, `^.{11,16}$` is the primary-sourced pattern to use.

schemes.label: Codice Univoco Ufficio (IPA)
schemes.helpText: 6-character 'Codice Ufficio' looked up on indicepa.gov.it — only a Pubblica Amministrazione has one. Needed so a domestic invoice to a government client routes as FPA12, not FPR12/XXXXXXX.

provenance.sourceText: «CodiceDestinatario: identifica il soggetto al quale è destinata la fattura; - nei casi di fattura destinata ad una Pubblica Amministrazione il suo valore, di 6 caratteri, deve corrispondere a quello presente nel campo Codice Ufficio riportato nella rubrica "Indice PA" (WWW.INDICEPA.GOV.IT).»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. Line wraps closed and typographic quotes normalised in the quotation above; wording unchanged. appliesTo COMPANY: only a Pubblica Amministrazione holds a Codice Ufficio in IndicePA, and this product records a government client as `Client.kind === 'GOVERNMENT'` on a COMPANY-shaped record -- there is no INDIVIDUAL-shaped government body. required false: the scheme is effectively mandatory, but only for the GOVERNMENT subset, an axis `appliesTo` cannot express (it distinguishes party TYPE, not `kind`). `b2g-routing/data/it.json` already enforces the real requirement for that subset at send time. Requiring it here would block saving an ordinary Italian business client that will never be a PA. pattern: 6 alphanumeric characters, from "il suo valore, di 6 caratteri" above, cross-checked against the same document's length table at par. 3.2 ("lunghezza che va da 6 a 7 caratteri" -- 6 is the PA branch, 7 the non-PA one). Case-insensitive because `fatturapa-provider.ts` uppercases before emitting CodiceDestinatario.

schemes.label: Codice Destinatario (SdI)
schemes.helpText: 7-character code the Sistema di Interscambio assigns on request ('Richiesta codici destinatario B2B' on fatturapa.gov.it) to a non-PA recipient with an accredited receiving channel. Needed so a domestic B2B/private invoice routes to the right mailbox instead of falling back to a placeholder.

provenance.sourceText: «CodiceDestinatario: identifica il soggetto al quale è destinata la fattura; [...] - nei casi di fattura destinata ad un soggetto diverso da Pubblica Amministrazione il suo valore, di 7 caratteri, deve corrispondere a: uno dei codici che il Sistema di Interscambio attribuisce ai soggetti, con canale accreditato in ricezione, che ne abbiano fatto richiesta attraverso la funzione "Richiesta codici destinatario B2B" presente sul sito WWW.FATTURAPA.GOV.IT; [...]»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Same document, fetch and date as the IT_PA_CODE fact above. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. Line wraps closed and typographic quotes normalised in the quotation above; wording unchanged. appliesTo BOTH, not COMPANY: the quoted text gates this branch on "un soggetto diverso da Pubblica Amministrazione" with no further qualifier, so an individual holding an accredited receiving channel is as eligible as a company; COMPANY-only would silently under-declare for an INDIVIDUAL-typed client. required false: no seller can compel a buyer to hold or disclose an SdI code it may never have requested, and the specification itself provides two further fallbacks (PEC, then '0000000'/'XXXXXXX') for exactly that case -- which would be senseless were it mandatory. pattern: 7 alphanumeric characters, from "il suo valore, di 7 caratteri" above, cross-checked against the par. 3.2 length table. Case-insensitive, matching the provider's own uppercasing.

schemes.label: PEC (Posta Elettronica Certificata)
schemes.helpText: Certified email address used as the SdI delivery channel when the recipient has no Codice Destinatario (SdI) on file. Only used for a non-PA recipient.

provenance.sourceText: «PECDestinatario: indirizzo di Posta Elettronica Certificata al quale viene recapitata la fattura; viene valorizzato nei soli casi di destinatario diverso da Pubblica Amministrazione, qualora il destinatario utilizzi il canale PEC per ricevere le fatture. Può essere valorizzato solo se il valore di CodiceDestinatario è uguale a '0000000'.» Same par. 1.1, on the CodiceDestinatario branch itself: «'0000000', nei casi di fattura destinata ad un soggetto che riceve tramite PEC e questa sia indicata nel campo PECDestinatario;»

schemes.notes: Specifiche tecniche operative del formato della fattura del Sistema di Interscambio v1.3.2 (Allegato A del DM 55/2013), Agenzia delle Entrate, par. 1.1. Same document, fetch and date as the IT_PA_CODE fact above. Primary text: https://www.fatturapa.gov.it/export/documenti/Specifiche_tecniche_del_formato_FatturaPA_V1.3.2.pdf fetched 2026-09-13 (curl with a browser User-Agent, HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1 190 498 bytes) and read with `pdftotext -layout`, never a fetch-summary. Line wraps closed and typographic quotes normalised in the quotation above; wording unchanged. appliesTo BOTH and required false for the same reasons as IT_SDI: the text gates on a non-PA recipient without restricting to businesses, and this is the SECOND fallback, reached only when no SdI code exists. NO pattern on purpose: the specification's length table at par. 3.2 states only "formato alfanumerico; lunghezza che va da 7 a 256 caratteri" -- a length range, not an email grammar. Declaring a generic address regex would be a formal claim no primary source here supports, which this catalog's provenance discipline forbids.

notes:
Italy, five schemes. VAT and LEGAL_ID are both `required: false` because this catalog's `appliesTo` axis is party TYPE, while Italy's buyer-side rule (DPR 633/1972 art. 21 comma 2 lettera f) turns on whether the buyer is a taxable person -- a distinction the schema does not carry, and which the DB's one-row-per-(country, scheme) shape cannot express as two role-scoped facts. Requiring either would hard-block a lawful client record. Each fact's own notes state the asymmetry in full.

IT_PA_CODE, IT_SDI and PEC are declared here because `formats/national/fatturapa-provider.ts` reads all three off the client to route FormatoTrasmissione and CodiceDestinatario, and this catalog is the only thing that makes a field for them exist: `client-upsert.tsx` renders one input per scheme declared for the party's country, keying its data-cy off `req.scheme` with no allowlist. While they were undeclared, a domestic Italian B2B client could not have its SdI code entered anywhere and fell through to CodiceDestinatario 'XXXXXXX' -- the value this same specification reserves for a recipient "non residente, non stabilito, non identificato in Italia". A domestic invoice announced to SdI as a foreign one.

`b2g-routing/data/it.json` separately declares IT_PA_CODE as mandatory for GOVERNMENT clients. The two are not duplicates: this catalog makes the field EXIST on any Italian record, that one makes it REQUIRED for that subset at send time.
